title: Deleting a user keeps their articles and sets author_id to NULL.
content:
The articles.author_id foreign key uses ondelete="SET NULL" and is nullable. Comments, favorites and follows use CASCADE instead, so they are removed with the user.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108

title: articlesCount in list responses is the length of the returned page, not the total match count.
content:
list_articles sets articles_count=len(articles) after the limited query. The feed route does the same, so clients cannot compute total pages from it.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:49

title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
content:
A module-level CryptContext with schemes=["bcrypt"] does both hashing and verification. deprecated="auto" is set on the context.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

title: API models expose camelCase JSON field names generated from snake_case attributes.
content:
RWModel sets alias_generator to convert_field_to_camel_case and allow_population_by_field_name, so fields like articles_count serialize as articlesCount. All domain models and schemas inherit RWModel.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:21

title: Article lists default to 20 items per page with limit/offset paging and no maximum.
content:
DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT is 20 and DEFAULT_ARTICLES_OFFSET is 0. Limit is only constrained by ge=1, so there is no upper bound in the code.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:8

title: Creating an article whose slug already exists is rejected with 400 instead of generating a new slug.
content:
create_new_article computes the slug, calls check_article_exists, and raises 400 ARTICLE_ALREADY_EXISTS if found. The articles.slug column is also unique in the migration.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:65

title: A separately stored per-user salt is prepended to the password before bcrypt hashing.
content:
change_password generates a salt with bcrypt.gensalt, stores it in the salt column, and hashes salt + password. check_password must prepend the same stored salt, so the salt column cannot be dropped without breaking logins.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24

title: Login returns the same 400 error for an unknown email and a wrong password.
content:
The login route builds one wrong_login_error with INCORRECT_LOGIN_INPUT and raises it both when the email lookup fails and when check_password fails. Callers cannot tell which input was wrong.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:30

title: Access tokens are signed with the symmetric HS256 algorithm.
content:
The JWT service fixes ALGORITHM to HS256 and uses it both to encode tokens and as the only accepted algorithm on decode. The same secret_key signs and verifies.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

title: Access tokens expire one week after issue.
content:
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is 60 * 24 * 7 and is passed as the expires_delta for every user token. There is no refresh token in the code.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

title: The JWT identifies the user by username only, not by user id.
content:
The token payload is built from JWTUser(username=...), and the auth dependency loads the user with get_user_by_username from the decoded claim. Renaming a user therefore invalidates their existing tokens.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29

title: Article ownership is checked by comparing author username with the current user's username.
content:
check_user_can_modify_article compares article.author.username to user.username, not ids. The update and delete routes depend on this check and return 403 when it fails.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

title: Database access uses raw SQL files loaded with aiosql on asyncpg, not an ORM.
content:
queries.py loads every .sql file in the sql folder through aiosql with the asyncpg driver, and repositories call these named queries. Dynamic article filtering is built separately with pypika.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5

title: An article slug is derived from its title with slugify and nothing else.
content:
get_slug_for_article returns slugify(title) with no suffix, id or random part. Two articles with titles that slugify the same get the same slug.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:19

title: Updating an article title regenerates its slug, so the article URL changes.
content:
update_article_by_slug computes a new slug when the update contains a title and passes it to the repository. Unlike create, this path does not check for an existing article with the new slug.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:100

title: The Authorization header must use the prefix "Token", not "Bearer".
content:
Settings default jwt_token_prefix to "Token". The auth dependency splits the header on a space and returns 403 WRONG_TOKEN_PREFIX if the prefix differs.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

title: updated_at is maintained by a PostgreSQL trigger, not by application code.
content:
The migration creates the plpgsql function update_updated_at_column, which sets NEW.updated_at = now(), and attaches it as a BEFORE UPDATE trigger on users, articles and commentaries.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27
